registration_read.verdict: Same split as plate 1, on a plate whose own reference this model generated four minutes earlier: the FAR plane registers, the three isolated-object planes do not.
by_object: far (sky/water/crane/ground) REGISTERS: the gantry crane's dark mass falls at x~960-1150, on the reference's crane, the horizon matches and the +-42 px correlation search finds no better shift than (0,0). It drops the reference's mooring bollards and the left-hand warehouse post, which arguably belong to this plane.

mid (containers/dock lamps) DOES NOT REGISTER: delivered opaque with a painted checkerboard. Attempt 1 drew one centred bank; the re-roll split it into a left and a right bank, closer to the reference's arrangement but still inboard of the reference's edge-to-edge container walls.

subject (desk/ledger/stool) DOES NOT REGISTER: the re-roll returned true alpha (the only transparent asset of this plate). Alpha bbox x 69-1417, y 153-960 (1348x807 px) against the reference group read at roughly x 230-860, y 610-1000 (about 630x390 px): about 2.1x too large and lifted some 450 px; the stool moves from beside the desk to in front of it.

near (hanging lamp) DOES NOT REGISTER: delivered opaque with a painted checkerboard. Measured on the shade's own ink, it spans x 379-816 against the reference lamp's x 414-629 - about 1.9x too wide, centre about +67 px right - and the cable enters the top edge at the wrong column.
registration_read.translation_search: far best offset (0,0); subject and near saturate the +-42 px search; mid's best fit (0,-26) is the painted checkerboard correlating with the sky, not a match.

style_drift_read: Style holds across all four and against the reference plate: the same dusk palette (steel-blue sky, copper horizon band, teal/orange containers, charcoal ink), the same flat woodblock register, the same ink weight, no banned gradients. No palette drift worth naming. The drift that matters is positional.
route_finding: Through the claims pipeline the generating agent's only image capability is codex's built-in image_gen.imagegen. It exposes NO model, quality, size or background parameter: the model that actually generated is gpt-image 2.0 (read from the delivered PNG's C2PA metadata), not GPT Image 2.5, and 'transparent background' can only be asked for in prose. Asked in prose, the model PAINTS a checkerboard instead of returning alpha: 6 of 9 delivered assets came back opaque RGB with a drawn grey/white checkerboard, and only 2 of 6 transparent slots ever returned a real alpha channel (1 on attempt 1, 1 on the single re-roll).
alpha_clean_rule: Cleaned only the true-alpha assets: alpha<=12 (a stray veil) and half-transparent pixels that are near-white (min channel >=248) or near-black (max <=6) go to alpha 0; the antialias rim is kept (doc 24). Opaque deliveries were NOT hand-matted (brief rule).
